newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO official compares Netanyahu vision to Nazi era.
newsitem.headline: PLO official compares Netanyahu vision to Nazi era.

text.p: A senior Palestinian official on Wednesday likened Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's vision of a permanent peace settlement with the Palestinians to the Nazi era.
Netanyahu laid out for the first time to his security cabinet his permanent settlement blueprint in which Israel would keep key areas in the occupied West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem.
Asked for his reaction to the proposal, Palestinian Finance Minister Mohammed al-Nashashibi told Israel Television:
"It never happened in modern history that one will... confiscate 23 percent of another state land claiming that it is necessary for defence...that was only presented by the Nazis."
Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan rejected the comparison, calling it an "obscenity".

"Any talk of Israel taking land of another nation is sheer nonsense. Mr Nashashibi doesn't seem to realise that according to international law Israel's claim to this land is more valid than any others and the use of an analogy to the Nazis is nothing but an obscenity," Bar-Illan said.
Six million Jews were murdered in Nazi death camps during World War Two.
Earlier Palestinian President Yasser Arafat rejected the Israeli plan as a violation of the 1993 peace agreement.
"This is completely against the peace process and against the agreement," Arafat told reporters on his return to the Gaza Strip from Cairo.
Under the Netanyahu plan, Israel would keep full control of "Greater Jerusalem", including a bloc of Jewish settlements to the south, and the Jordan Valley, the source said.
Israel would also control other blocs of settlements in the West Bank as well as "vital roads", the source added.

Under Israeli-Palestinian peace deals the fate of the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem, will be decided during permanent settlement negotiations. The talks have been suspended since Netanyahu came to power a year ago.
